text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- The paper publishes the first of several exerpts of a forthcoming book by Andi Meister, the former head of the three nation commission set up to investigate the causes of the 1994 Estonia ferry disaster.
- The Home Enhancing Central Council, formed on Vormsi island on Friday, is to lead the countrywide home enhancment campaign, initiated by President Lennart Meri.
- The largest exposition hall in the Baltics, with 5,000 square metres of space, will be finished by the autumn, the finance director of Eesti Naitused, Helle Kallas, said.
- Lithuanian President Algirdas Brazauskas said in an interview he probably would not run in the next presidential election.
- Police detained five men suspected of robbing Hoiupank's Saku office, and found 120,000 kroons 700,000 that was stolen.
- The Legal Translation Centre in Tallinn, financed by the European Union PHARE programme, is expanding to to ensure that 50,000 pages of documents will be translated on time.
- Ex-prime minister Tiit Vahi says he is considering buying shares in the rare earths plant Silmet.
